scope: The original seven-witness predicate and unchanged 24-squaring anchor only; no approval of the full polynomial or five-contact geometry.

sources.author: Joseph H. Silverman
sources.title: The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves

applications.conclusion: The literal seven-witness formula defines Z_(2) intersect Z_(3).
hypotheses_and_conventions: a=2 and b=3 are nonzero rationals.
i^2=a, j^2=b, ij=-ji; norm is x0^2-a*x1^2-b*x2^2+a*b*x3^2 and trace is 2*x0.
The paper's T is S+S without Poonen's finite offset.
Hilbert symbols computed at 2,3,all other odd primes and infinity give exactly ramification set {2,3}.
The real interval convention in Proposition 6 is irrelevant because infinity is split.
Recover v0=(t-2*u0)/2; clearing the fixed denominator 2 gives exactly the archive's second equation.

applications.conclusion: Integral multiplication series on the formal branch have linear term n*z; oddness for this Weierstrass model gives [3]z=3z+O(z^3).
hypotheses_and_conventions: The coefficients 11-6*sqrt(2) belong to the local integer ring at both 2 and 3.
Use z=-x/y and w=-1/y, with w=z^3-(11-6*sqrt(2))*z*w^2.
The formal construction requires integral Weierstrass coefficients, not a minimal model assertion at 2.
Negation is (x,y)->(x,-y), hence z->-z, so multiplication series are odd in characteristic zero.
At 3 the initial point 2P is in the formal kernel at depth 1; higher odd terms have strictly greater valuation than 3z.
At 2 the displayed x and y valuations put P on the formal branch; small z alone would not suffice.

applications.conclusion: For nonzero S=nP, the literal anchor holds exactly when n lies in 2*3^(2^23-1)Z.
